Criterion: Potential life-threatening injury or uncontrolled hazardous vehicle response with little practical mitigation
Evidence_Prompt: Hazard linkage; vehicle effect; safety-goal relevance; operating scenario

Criterion: Potential serious injury, loss of safety-critical function, or major safety-related noncompliance
Evidence_Prompt: Safety analysis; regulatory interface; warning and mitigation assumptions

Criterion: Primary function is lost, vehicle/product becomes inoperable, or immediate controlled shutdown is required
Evidence_Prompt: Functional architecture; safe or degraded state definition

Criterion: Major function is significantly degraded, continued use is restricted, or immediate service is required
Subsystem remains available with clear performance, availability, or operating-range reduction
Function remains available but customer experiences clear performance or convenience loss
Limited performance deviation with practical workaround and no material risk
Noticeable effect without meaningful loss of intended function
Barely perceptible effect that does not change normal use
No credible customer, vehicle, manufacturing, or downstream functional effect
Cause is active in normal conditions and failure is routinely reproduced
Evidence_Prompt: Repeated normal-condition test or field evidence

Criterion: Cause is commonly encountered and requires little combination of conditions
Evidence_Prompt: High-frequency data; weak margin; dominant mechanism

Criterion: Failure repeats across builds, units, environments, or operating cycles
Failure occurs in a defined but regularly encountered operating scenario
Credible cause has appeared in test, production, supplier, or field evidence
Cause is credible but requires a limited combination of conditions or has sparse evidence
Evidence_Prompt: Boundary test; early-life data; mechanism analysis

Criterion: Cause requires multiple contributing conditions or is strongly reduced by design/process margin
Cause is physically credible only near unusual or extreme conditions
Mechanism is difficult to realize within the validated operating envelope
Evidence_Prompt: Robust margin; no observed events; capability evidence

Criterion: No credible cause remains after design review, analysis, and representative validation
No prevention or detection control exists before exposure
Issue is most likely discovered through complaint, field failure, or teardown
Sampling or limited inspection may detect the issue but escape probability remains high
Detection depends heavily on operator judgment, visual inspection, setup, or exact conditions
Automated control exists but does not cover full fault population or operating range
Evidence_Prompt: Coverage gaps; test limits; missed-fault analysis

Criterion: Controls detect many cases but boundary, timing, or latent-fault gaps remain
Automated detection is repeatable, limits are controlled, and reaction is defined
Functionally independent monitor detects the fault within required time and controls the reaction
Independent prevention and detection layers cover the fault with periodic proof or self-test
Evidence_Prompt: Layered coverage; proof-test interval; dependency review

Criterion: Cause is prevented by design or detected automatically with validated near-complete coverage and controlled reaction
